title: A King Shall Reign in Righteousness
description: A King Shall Reign in Righteousness in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Sebastian Streeter wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 255 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Hiding-place”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A King shall reign in right-eous-ness, And all the kin-dred na-tions bless; The King of Sa-lem, King of peace, Nor shall his spread-ing king-dom cease.

lines: A King shall reign in righteousness,
And all the kindred nations bless;
The King of Salem, King of peace, —
Nor shall his spreading kingdom cease.
In him the naked soul shall find
Or, when the raging tempests beat,
A covert warm, a safe retreat.
In burning sands and thirsty ground,
He like a river shall be found,
Or lofty rock, beneath whose shade
The weary traveller rests his head.
The dimness gone, all eyes shall see
All ears shall hearken, and the word
Of life receive from Christ the Lord.

licence: Public domain: Sebastian Streeter died in 1867.
credits: Words by Sebastian Streeter (1783–1867), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
